prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Revise the ORIGINAL v01 activated Rest Assured scene supplied as input. The owner prefers this earlier chair; keep its design, soft aqua upholstery, molded ivory shell, circular side pivots, base and welcoming1960s product aesthetic. The later upright donut-shaped rings were rejected as mechanically illogical. Do NOT make upright camera-facing ring/eye shapes. Make the activated state clearly different from the inviting chair through LOGICAL restraint placement and a modest pose adjustment.

MECHANICAL PLACEMENT: A seated person's elbows would be near the chair back, with forearms resting lengthwise along the padded armrests toward the front. Therefore place ONE CLOSED PADDED CUFF ACROSS THE FRONT THIRD OF EACH ARMREST, just behind where the hand would overhang, NOT near the elbow/backrest. Each is a LOW curved aqua padded cap closing sideways onto a shallow cream-lined wrist cradle recessed in the TOP of the existing armrest. Its two ends visibly seat into the armrest sides with one small ivory latch on the outer side. The empty wrist channel runs ALONG THE ARMREST toward the chair front/legrest, NOT toward the camera as a freestanding donut. It is a complete closed cuff physically anchored to the armrest, NOT an open U arch, bridge over the elbow area, upright ring standing on a pole, cuff over the seat, or loose unattached clamp. The padded cap and lower cradle enclose a small EMPTY wrist gap; no body part. At native314x206 the pads should read clearly as a couple of firm soft clamps holding the wrist-rest positions. Remove the old high rearward arch shapes and restore smooth ordinary padding there. Route short locked links from the cuff mounts to the existing side mechanism; make their lock tabs/latch joins visible, no robot arms. Keep everything compact and comfortable-looking.

POSE: keep the SAME room camera, chair footprint and object proportions; recline the same backrest only about8-12degrees further and lift its SAME integrated legrest slightly closer to level, with the side adjustment linkage visibly locked. Keep the whole chair within the existing framing; do not enlarge, move the base or add a separate footstool. The raised legrest and reclined back plus front-positioned closed padded cuffs should distinguish this activated state from a merely inviting lounge recliner.

Keep the small picked-at seam at the FRONT OUTER END of the viewer-LEFT armrest: short dark stitch break and tiny cream tuft visible at native size, without a large tear. Maintain infinity/green status display. Absolutely NO hands, wrists, legs, human shadow, person, body, gore, spikes, torture-machine styling, corpse, face, text or UI. Preserve the ORIGINAL room, sofa/coral cushion, window/garden, doorway/dining glimpse, lights, floor/rug, cabinet and especially approved rectangular flush wall intercom unchanged. No plant edits. Deliberate chunky pixel art on exactly314x206 opaque canvas, aspect157:103, hard-edge controlled clusters, same original colors, no new texture/dither/blur. Local chair-geometry change only; not a full-room redesign.
refinementPrompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Input1 is the corrected activated chair with LOW CUFFS AT THE FRONT WRIST RESTS, a modest further recline and raised legrest. (2) Keep the original compact IVORY BASE footprint shown in input2, rather than extending a new broad base under the raised legrest. The legrest lift exposes red rug/floor under its front portion. Same chair/base product as original, no new forward plinth or footstool. Preserve the slight further recline, raised SAME legrest, chair camera position, original aqua/ivory colors, segmented padding, picked front-left armrest seam and infinity/green display. Room, architecture, sofa, window/garden, cabinet, doorway and flush intercom unchanged. No people or anatomy, spikes, gore, added mechanisms, text, UI or modern styling.
